title: Graphene-coated sphere
note: The full solution with a conducting sheet on the sphere against the quasi-static resonance condition: they meet as R → 0 and part by retardation, too little to see here (5e-5 at 5 nm, 9e-4 at 60 nm); the test asserts the shift stays within (kR)².
summary: the plasmon resonance against its quasi-static position
aside:
A conducting sheet σ on a sphere of radius R shifts the resonance of order ℓ to where, in the quasi-static limit,

$$\mathrm{Re}\left[\varepsilon_1 \ell + \varepsilon_2 (\ell + 1) + \frac{i\sigma\,\ell(\ell+1)\,\lambda}{2\pi R}\right] = 0.$$

PyStratify's full solution with the sheet (graphene, $E_F$ = 0.5 eV, ε = 2.1 inside, 1.77 outside) finds the peak of |T₁|; the two meet as $R \to 0$ and part by retardation, within $(kR)^2$ as the test asserts.
